correctness.rationale: Every unallocated A chore forces each recipient to possess a B chore, so no A chore can be assigned and all B chores must be assigned; the symmetric case completes the exhaustive maximality trichotomy. Uniform chore EF1 is precisely a bundle-size spread of at most one. The factorial census follows from uniquely determined A recipient sets and multinomial allocations. If neither side has at least n chores, a full equitable allocation is constructed using one/two jobs per agent or singletons. The optimal throughput law follows; \(K_{2h-1,2h+1}\) with four agents gives the sharp limiting 1/2 bound. Direct brute force checks 63 entire finite cells, 726261 assignment states; no finite search is invoked as proof of infinite assertions.

originality.rationale: The complete-equitable-coloring subproblem is explicitly credited to established equitable coloring literature. The distinct new assessed theorem is the exact disjoint classification of incomplete inclusion-maximal EF1 allocations, its labeled complete-plus-incomplete census and the sharp optimal-throughput law. Inspected 2024/2025/2026 conflict allocation research focuses on general existence/complexity or path/interval graph cases, not this exact biclique partial-allocation census. Searches located potentially related graph coloring/packing results but no statement implying the partial EF1 trichotomy plus throughput; equivalence outside indexed primary works remains a risk.
residual_risks: Exact maximal partial equitable colorings may have been studied under other terminology in unindexed combinatorics or scheduling sources.
Not every article, revision, bibliography reference or inaccessible publication was exhaustively read.
The complete equitable-colorability criterion alone is prior work, and is not independently novel.

value.rationale: The original problem is how much work can be completed while respecting EF1 and insertion maximality under natural task conflicts. The theorem answers this optimization question exactly for every population and side size, enumerates the full solution space and identifies an asymptotically sharp nearly-50-percent lost-throughput phenomenon with only four agents. This is more than an existence restatement or a toy numerical gain, and exposes a concrete structural tension between complete equitable coloring and maximal partial fairness.
